question.text: The first Persian invasion of Greece was led by this Persian ruler in order to punish them for their participation in the Ionian Revolt. This man divided his empire into satraps.
question.clue: This leader of an expedition against the Scythians divided his empire into twenty satrapies, and he built a noted network of roads.

swap.leadin: This ruler founded the Achaemenid [ah-KEE-men-id] Empire, which successfully grew by supporting local rulers as satraps and respecting local customs.
swap.text: Name this "Great" Persian ruler of the sixth century BCE who ended the Babylonian Captivity.
swap.clue: This father of Cambyses II denounced his foe Nabonidus in a namesake cuneiform document, having earlier defeated Astyages and taken Ecbatana, breaking away from Median rule.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the SAVAK secret police force.
question.text: SAVAK was active in this country until its 1979 revolution, which saw the overthrow of its Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. More than 50 Americans were held hostage in this country's city of Tehran.
question.answerHtml: Iran [or Islamic Republic of Iran or Jomhuri-ye Eslami-ye Iran; accept Iranian Revolution]
question.clue: This country was invaded by neighboring Iraq to limit the power of its Shia majority.

swap.text: Leonidas' 300 Spartans were defeated by this empire's much larger force: over 2 million troops if you believe Herodotus, which scholars don't. Xerxes [zerk-zees] led this empire against the Greeks, but was defeated at the naval Battle of Salamis.
swap.clue: One ruler of this empire famously ordered the ocean to be whipped.

question.leadin: Answer the following about civilizations that relied on horse archers.
question.text: Retreating horse archers would turn around to shoot arrows at the enemy in a "shot" named for this empire. This Persian empire between that of the Seleucids and the Sassanids used horse archers in their defeat of Crassus at the Battle of Carrhae.
question.answerHtml: Parthian Empire [accept Arsacid dynasty or empire; accept Parthian shot]
question.clue: An early use of the word "philhellene" , meaning "lover of the Greeks," was on the coins of this empire's Mithridates I , who was descended from the 3rd-century BC founder after whom this empire is sometimes named.

swap.leadin: After the Iberian War in 532, this empire signed the Perpetual Peace with a neighbor to its west.
swap.text: Name this empire whose leader Khosrow I signed that treaty. Procopius, a neighboring empire's most famous historian, recorded that the treaty was broken within a decade in the Lazic War.
swap.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

question.text: According to the Chronicle of Early Kings, Sargon defeated an attempted invasion by four "great" generals from this polity, which was led by the King of Awan.
question.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

swap.leadin: This man named 16 cities after his father, Antiochus.
swap.text: Name this general who served under a famous Macedonian king during his Asian campaigns. He was also the first ruler of a namesake empire, the easternmost of the Macedonian successor states.
swap.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

question.text: By dethroning his grandfather Astyages, Cyrus ended this empire, which was led from Ecbatana. Under Cyaxares, this empire took part in the conquest of Neo-Assyria.
question.clue: As a result of a battle at the Halys River, that waterway was declared its border with Lydia.

swap.leadin: The Hall of Hundred Columns in this city has the same dimensions as Athens's Odeon.
swap.text: Identify this ceremonial capital in the Zagros Mountains, home to the Apadana Palace built by Darius I.
swap.clue: In this home of a hundred-columned throne room, the Gate of All Nations led to the apadana palace.

question.leadin: A ruler with this name had the Lakhmid king Al Nu'man III executed.
question.text: Give this name of a Sassanid shahanshah who then annexed the Lakhmid kingdom. An earlier shahanshah of this name went to war with Justinian after his allies raided the Lakhmids, who were then Sassanid vassals.
question.answerHtml: Khosrau [accept Khosrau I, Khosrau II, Khosrau Anushirawan, Khosrau the Just, or Chosroes]
question.clue: The second Sassanid ruler with this name held a truce with the Byzantine Empire because of his friendship with the Emperor Maurice, which lasted until Maurice was killed. The first began an "Eternal Peace" because of a bribe from Justinian, which lasted until that ruler got bored.

swap.leadin: One account says this ruler died while fighting Queen Tomyris and her Massagetae people.
swap.text: Name this ruler, whose son and successor was Cambyses II. He defeated the Babylonians at the battle of Opis and his Edict of Restoration ended the Israelites' Babylonian captivity.
swap.answerHtml: Cyrus II [accept Cyrus the Great or Cyrus the Elder]
swap.clue: This man defeated Nabonidus at the Battle of the Opis and bested Croesus at the Battle of Thymbra to conquer the Lydian Empire.

question.text: Many Neo-Hittite states to the south spoke this Semitic language that replaced Akkadian to become the lingua franca of the Near East
question.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

swap.leadin: Herodotus claimed that couriers travelling along this thing were not stopped by "snow nor rain nor heat nor gloom of night"
swap.text: Name this highway built by Darius I, which ran from Susa to Sardis. This highway contained mud brick stops known as chapar khaneh, which were used by couriers to change horses.
swap.clue: This Achaemenid public works project linked Susa, a capital in modern-day Iran, to Sardis in Anatolia. It allowed horse-mounted mail couriers to go super-fast.

question.text: This Sassanid city was the site of an A.D. 363 battle that took place between Shapur II and Emperor Julian, which saw a tactical victory for the Romans. It was the primary capital for both the Parthian and Sassanid Empires.
question.clue: This city was known by Arabs as "al- Mada'in" or "the cities" due to its many suburbs, one of which was sarcastically dubbed "better than Antioch," while another was home to the patriarch of the Nestorian church.

swap.text: An image of the false Smerdis kneeling before Darius the Great can be found on this rock inscription in Kermanshah Province. Henry Rawlinson was the first to translate the writing on this rock relief.
swap.answerHtml: Behistun Inscription [accept the Bisutun Inscription; or the Bisotun Inscription; or the Bagastana Inscription; or the Bisitun Inscription]
swap.clue: This document justifies the position of the ruler who ordered it created by claiming that he saved the kingdom from the possibly fictional usurper Gaumata.

question.leadin: Its capital was known as Ecbatana to the Greeks, and was probably founded by Cyaxeres.
question.text: Name this empire, whose last ruler Astyages was overtrown by Cyrus the Great.
question.clue: The city of Nineveh was captured by his successor Cyaxares, who extended this kingdom's borders to the Halys river in Asia Minor.

swap.leadin: A ruler with this name founded and named a city which was the location of an academy that served as the inspiration for Baghdad's House of Wisdom.
swap.text: Give this name of the son of Ardashir I, who captured the Roman emperor Valerian during his campaigns to expand the Sassanid Empire westward.
swap.clue: A king with this name built a namesake city on the road between Estakhr and Ctesiphon.

question.text: Parthian rule ended after this local ruler of Istakhr overthrew Artabanus V and established the Sassanid Empire. This father of Shapur I built a namesake palace as well as the Maiden Castle in the city of Fars, and skirmished with Alexander Severus's forces to the West.
question.clue: This man, whose early life is the subject of a "book of deeds" or Kar-Namag written in Middle Persian, was the son of a lord of Fars named Papak.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the last Himyarite king, Abraha's son Ma'd-Karib.
swap.text: Ma'd Karib was assisted by this Sassanid shahanshah during a later Axumite invasion of Himyar, which saw this monarch's general Vahrez win the Battle of Hadhramaut. Earlier, he concluded the Eternal Peace with Justinian the Great.
swap.clue: This Sasanian emperor who succeeded Kavad I. Most historians believe that Yemen came under Sassanid rule during his reign.
